free_text: A biopsy is recommended because the patient presents with a PI-RADS score of 4 on MRI and a rising PSA trend from 2.3 ng/mL to 2.5 ng/mL. Although the documented Gleason grade is missing, the combination of a high-risk imaging finding and rising PSA trajectory necessitates further clarification of the prior biopsy status. The evidence converged on the need for further tissue diagnosis to guide management.
